newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola up in line with stronger CBOT soybeans.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola up in line with stronger CBOT soybeans.

text.p: WCE canola futures rose on the heels on stronger CBOT soybean prices and export interest from the Far East, traders said.
"Canola was up on the Chicago market," a trader said. "We are seeing some export interest in canola which is supportive."
Local and commercial buying pushed January canola $2.60 to bid at $404.00 a tonne and March gained $2.20 to bid at $403.80 at 1108 CST.
On the minus side, there was some scale-up selling by commercials and farmer hedging, the trader said.
Flax, buoyed by higher canola, was mainly up due to the lack of selling and commercial buying. January flax jumped $2.30 to bid at $350.00 a tonne.
Rising CBOT wheat and corn prices also contributed to Monday's gains in western barley and feed wheat, traders said.
Commercial buying was also prevalent in the feed grains, a trader said.
February western barley firmed $0.60 to bid at $135.00 a tonne and March feed wheat gained $1.40 to $169.30.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
